examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Velocity Vector of a Particle Moving in Two Dimensions at a Given Time
examples.problem:
The position vector $\mathbf{r}$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t > 0$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle 12t, 2t^3\rangle.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $\mathbf{v}$ at time $t=1.$
examples.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨12,6{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=1$, we substitute into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨12,6(1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨12,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
A particle $P$ is moving in the $x$-$y$ plane. Its position vector relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by

$$
r=⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v.$

$v=⟨${{field-1}}$\,,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-12\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-12\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$
